product_structure_summary._note: High-level map of Third System's offering structure. The detailed specs for each product live in the 'documents' block below. This summary is the navigation layer.

layer_1_public_research.purpose: Free, citable artifacts that establish Third System as a known research practice. Generate inbound flow that feeds Layer 3.
layer_1_public_research.audience: CMOs, brand strategists, journalists, academic peers, prospective clients
layer_1_public_research.commercial_role: No transaction. Builds authority and credibility.

layer_2_methodology_and_frameworks.purpose: Free intellectual property published openly to establish that the measurement is rigorous and peer-reviewable.
products: tri_system_book_and_paper (separate spec — not in this file)
layer_2_methodology_and_frameworks.audience: Academic peers, clients evaluating credibility, journalists fact-checking findings

layer_3_commercial_diagnostics.purpose: Paid client engagements. The only revenue layer currently active.
layer_3_commercial_diagnostics.audience: Paying clients (CMO, brand director, head of brand strategy)
layer_3_commercial_diagnostics.commercial_role: Generates revenue. Pricing per AI Brand Visibility Diagnostic Pilot: $10–15K initial, $20–30K post-validation, $40K+ later.

product_to_template_map._note: Each product maps to one InDesign template family. Products marked 'NOT InDesign' use other design tools (slides, book interior).

template_family_purposes.A-Snapshot: Single-page or 2-page communication. Front (1-col or 2-col) + Back layouts. Use for scan-and-share artifacts where the reader makes a quick engage/move-on decision.
template_family_purposes.B-Snapshot: The back side of A-Snapshot. Used in pair with A-Snapshot; not a standalone product family.
template_family_purposes.C-Brochure: Multi-page long-form report. Cover + body spreads. The flagship template family for any substantive publication. Most Third System reports use this.
template_family_purposes.E-Tri-fold: Single Letter sheet folded into 6 panels. Foldable physical artifact, suited to authority pieces designed for in-person distribution (conferences, SVA, client meetings).
template_family_purposes.0-Cover: Standalone cover treatments. Usable when a deliverable needs only a cover (rare). Not mapped to any current Third System product.
template_family_purposes._unused_families: The InDesign template includes additional master families (D-, F-, G- variants) not currently mapped to any Third System product. Don't introduce these until a product genuinely requires them — a smaller, intentionally-used template set is stronger than every possible layout half-used.

persona_logic._note: The InDesign template uses 'persona' to denote audience-tier variants of the same physical layout: Executive, Manager, Specialist. Third System maps these as follows.

executive_persona.tone: C-suite. Strategic implications first; methodological detail second.

manager_persona.tone: Operational. Clear findings, shareable up and across, light on theoretical framing.
manager_persona.default_body_master: A-Snapshot - Front - 2 Columns - Letter - Portrait + B-Snapshot - Back - Letter - Portrait

specialist_persona.tone: Technical. Methodology, registry construction, statistical caveats foregrounded.

production_sprint_sequence._note: Recommended build order. Not the same as production_priority_order below — that's a flat list. This is sprint-grouped so visual decisions cascade correctly.

sprint_1_foundation_visual_system.rationale: Sets the look. Every later product inherits the visual decisions made here. Build cross_category_report first; it carries the most weight.

products: category_snapshot (one per published category, ~5 to start)
sprint_2_outreach_material.rationale: Lets Pablo start conversations. Strategy doc Week 3 calls for outreach — these are the artifacts that get attached to those messages.

sprint_3_authority_artifact.rationale: Establishes peer-reviewable credibility. Distributable at SVA, conferences, in client evaluation conversations.

sprint_4_commercial_enablement.rationale: Built once a paid pilot is in conversation. Anonymized version of the client deliverable, sent when prospects ask 'what does the deliverable look like?'

sprint_5_sales_tool_when_warranted.rationale: Don't build until you have warm leads. Shape becomes clear from what prospects actually ask about.

deferred_until_triggered.rationale: Each has a specific trigger condition. Don't pre-build.

backfill.rule: Published reports are registered without re-rendering; a code appears on a PDF only from its next render. Every distinct report PDF that was published has its own code, numbered in order of publication: deposited on OSF (each OSF version counts) or served from the website's main branch. Copies whose pages are identical and differ only in metadata (the website's corrected Title fields, deterministic rebuilds) share one code and are listed under variants. Held studies (v0.38, v0.39) are on OSF only and marked held: true; they never go to the website.
backfill.sources: Read-only, Nov 13, 2026: the website repo (origin/main 5c8c873: public/files/reports and boards/Studies.dc.html), the aias repo (all refs, stash entries included) and the main tree's untracked report outputs, and the public OSF project ec6wh (file listing with SHA-256 for current versions; older versions downloaded and hashed).

fields.title: the report's title (the website's listing title where it matches the cover; site_title when the cover's differs)
fields.date: OSF deposit date (UTC) of this PDF; for a PDF never deposited, its own CreationDate
fields.tier: 1 Flagship, 2 Study, 3 Brief (third_system_brand.json publication_tiers); design says whether the PDF is in design system v2
fields.git_tag: the study's tag whose tree holds this exact PDF, or null
fields.git_commit: the first commit that holds these bytes
fields.osf_path: path in OSF project ec6wh (osfstorage); osf_version is the OSF file version
fields.sha256: SHA-256 of the PDF as published (the OSF copy where it was deposited)
fields.website: the website copy: path, SHA-256, first served (since) and site commit; path null when it has since been replaced
fields.variants: other published byte copies of the same revision (pages identical)
fields.status: current, or superseded by the study's next revision
